name: Delamere Forest Trails April
course: Marked forest routes on mixed trails.
transport: Runner parking at Whitefield Car Park, about 15 minutes from event village
facilities: Bag drop, course marshals and event village
rules: Carry route GPX as backup and check each distance's cut-off.
reason: A forest race with three substantially different distances. The parking walk and early 42K start make arrival more demanding than the race name suggests.

name: Delamere Forest Trails November
course: Forest, Sandstone Trail, Blakemere Moss and Old Pale Hill; 42K two laps.
transport: Delamere station near event village; runner parking about 15 minutes away
facilities: Bag drop, waymarking and aid stations
rules: The 42K passes the event village halfway; check November kit and route cut-offs.
reason: A late-autumn forest race where the 42K repeats a lap and has 637m published ascent. Rail access is near, but designated parking is a walk away.

name: Chasewater Trail Festival October
course: Lakeside paths, grass and woodland trail laps.
transport: Check paid parking and closing time at country park
facilities: Bag drop, event-village toilets and water for longer distances
rules: Verify the October race pack; the spring course is similar but conditions may differ.
reason: An autumn edition of the mixed-terrain Chasewater event. The half starts two hours before shorter routes; check car-park hours and route conditions.

name: Running GP Croft November
distance: Marathon / 20 miles / metric marathon / half marathon / 10 miles / 10km / 5km
transport: Croft Circuit, DL2 2PL; check access and parking
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village
rules: Metric marathon is 26.2km; confirm lap count and limit for your chosen race.
reason: The circuit removes traffic crossings but introduces repeated laps and seven staggered distances. The November edition warrants cold-weather preparation.

name: Run Aintree October
start: Check the exact wave for each distance.
course: Racecourse loop with tarmac and some trail path.
transport: Aintree station opposite venue; limited on-site parking
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and venue toilets
rules: Confirm lap count and final autumn event instructions.

name: Run Aintree May
course: Racecourse loop; mostly tarmac with a short trail section.
transport: Aintree station opposite venue; check Sunday services
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and venue toilets
rules: Check half-marathon limit and lap count before entry.
reason: A spring Aintree edition with late morning starts. It is a controlled loop but the trail segment and distance-specific laps should be considered for pacing.

name: Run Aintree July
course: Flat racecourse-ground route, with a short non-tarmac section.
transport: Rail station opposite Aintree; limited venue parking
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and water for 10K and half
rules: Summer 10:00 half start calls for weather and hydration planning.
reason: The July edition uses the same accessible racecourse setting as winter races, but the 10:00 half start creates a different heat and hydration decision.

name: Chepstow Running Festival August
start: Check the distance-specific August start times.
